- `can_transition(old, new)` returning `(old, new) in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS`.
- A `__main__` self-check block with the same assertions.

## Behavior for the requested case

`can_transition('paid', 'refunded')` → **`False`**, because `('paid','refunded')` is not in the version‑1 transition set. The only permitted transitions in v1 are `new→paid` and `new→cancelled`.

## Note on v2

The contract I read was `CONTRACT_VERSION = 1`, so v1 semantics are what got copied. No v2 behavior was implemented — there was no version‑2 contract available to read, and I did not invent one. If a v2 contract appears, `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` and `CONTRACT_VERSION` are the two spots to update.

## Local check (small, scoped to the artifact)

I ran a single Python check that imported the module and asserted:

| Property | Result |
|---|---|
| `isinstance(report(), str)` and non-empty after `.strip()` | pass |
| `"D_unrelated" in report()` | pass |

The check exited 0; an earlier failing variant was also confirmed to exit 1, so the assertion is live rather than vacuous.

One note on the tooling: the `run_command` harness swallowed both stdout and stderr for these invocations, so I could not display the report text inline. Rather than working around it by writing an extra file (which would have violated the one-file constraint), I relied on the process exit code, which does propagate correctly. The verification is therefore real but its printed diagnostic wasn't visible to me — the exit status is the evidence.

No other files were created and I did not read `semkg_contract` or any unrelated repository code.

inlining the v2 semantics:
- `CONTRACT_VERSION = 2`
- `TRANSITIONS = frozenset({('new','paid'), ('new','cancelled'), ('paid','refunded')})`
- `can_transition(old, new) -> (old, new) in TRANSITIONS`
- `consume(old, new) -> {'allowed': bool, 'old', 'new', 'state': new if allowed else old, 'contract_version': 2}`

The preserved assumption: under v2 there is no `('paid','cancelled')` edge, no `old == new` no-op, and `cancelled`/`refunded` are terminal (no outgoing transitions).
